answer.text: get_netrc_auth is defined in src/requests/utils.py at lines 231-280.
It returns a tuple of (login, password) for the given URL by looking up credentials in a netrc file.

rows.question: How does the library decide whether to keep the Authorization header when a redirect goes to a different host?

answer.text: The library strips the Authorization header when the redirect goes to a different hostname.
On the same host, it keeps the Authorization header for http-to-https redirects on standard ports (80 to 443).
It also keeps the header when the scheme hasn't changed and both old and new ports are default ports for that scheme.
Otherwise, if the scheme or port changes on the same host, the header is stripped.
The rebuild_auth method calls should_strip_auth and deletes the Authorization header when it returns True.

rows.question: Which hosts are excluded from using a proxy according to the environment configuration?

answer.text: The no_proxy environment variable defines hosts excluded from proxy usage, parsed by splitting on commas after removing spaces.
For IP addresses, exclusion matches exact IP or CIDR network notation in no_proxy.
For hostnames, exclusion matches exact hostname, hostname with port, or domain suffix with leading dot.

rows.question: How is the character encoding of a JSON response body detected from its raw bytes?

answer.text: When no encoding is set on the response, the JSON decoder calls guess_json_utf on the raw content bytes to detect the UTF encoding.
guess_json_utf examines the first four bytes of the data for byte order marks (BOMs) and null byte patterns to determine the encoding.
If no BOM is present, guess_json_utf counts null bytes in the sample and checks their positions to distinguish between UTF-8, UTF-16 (LE/BE), and UTF-32 (LE/BE).
If guess_json_utf returns an encoding, the JSON decoder attempts to decode the content with that encoding before falling back to the text property.
If JSON-specific detection fails or returns None, the decoder falls back to using self.text which relies on charset_normalizer or chardet for general encoding detection.

rows.question: timeout handling when the adapter sends a request

answer.text: HTTPAdapter.send normalizes the timeout parameter into a TimeoutSauce object with separate connect and read values before passing it to urllib3.
ConnectTimeout and ReadTimeout exceptions are raised from urllib3's MaxRetryError when the underlying connection or read operations exceed their respective timeout values.
The BaseAdapter.send method documents that timeout can be a float or a (connect timeout, read timeout) tuple.
Session.send delegates timeout handling to the adapter by passing the timeout parameter through kwargs to adapter.send.

rows.question: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable used for the verify setting

answer.text: When trust_env is enabled and verify is True or None, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable is checked first and used as the verify value if set.
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE takes precedence over CURL_CA_BUNDLE when both are set in the environment.
An empty REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE value is treated as unset and verify remains True.
The merged verify setting from merge_environment_settings is passed to the adapter's cert_verify method which uses it as a CA bundle path when not True.
Session.request calls merge_environment_settings with the verify parameter and uses the returned verify value for the actual request.

rows.question: when a POST is turned into a GET after a 302 or 303 redirect

answer.text: For a 303 (see_other) redirect, rebuild_method changes the request method to GET unless the method is HEAD.
For a 302 (found) redirect, rebuild_method changes the method to GET unless the method is HEAD, following browser behavior.
